record.paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Characterize signed simple graphs that have no chordless positive circles, or equivalently no chordless positive circles other than possibly triangles.

evidence.quote: Qn. 6. Characterize the signed simple graphs with no chordless positive circles. Or, with none other than triangles. Ans. ... the general questions are not at all easy.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $(G,\sigma)$ where $G=(V,E)$ is a simple undirected graph and $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$ is a sign function on its edges. The sign of a cycle (circle) $C$ in $(G,\sigma)$ is the product $\sigma(C)=\prod_{e\in E(C)}\sigma(e)$; the cycle is called positive if $\sigma(C)=+1$ and negative otherwise. A chord of a cycle $C$ in $G$ is an edge of $G$ whose two endpoints lie on $C$ but which is not itself an edge of $C$. A cycle is chordless (induced) if it has no chords.

Provide a structural characterization of the class of signed simple graphs $(G,\sigma)$ that contain no chordless positive cycle. Equivalently, give a structural characterization of signed simple graphs in which every chordless positive cycle (if any) is a triangle.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in Zaslavsky's problem collection on negative and positive circles in signed graphs, where it is explicitly stated as not easy and left without a known solution. No subsequent characterization theorem for signed simple graphs without chordless positive cycles was located in the literature; related questions about chordless negative cycles are also discussed as open. Status appears to remain open.
